Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Intro: baseline requirements + quick ask on procurement timing

Hi Sanjay / Anna —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I pulled together a short baseline of what we heard for MedCore's regulated workload:

- Multi-tenant isolation for PHI workloads (customer-managed VPC, private control plane)
- Requirement: SOC 2 + audited key management (KMS + HSM)
- Avg inference profile: 45M tokens/day with diurnal peak at ~12k qps for short-chat + 1k batch requests (up to 2048 tokens)
- SLO target: p95 latency < 150ms for interactive; batch throughput SLA for nightly billing jobs

Attached is the requirement doc and a draft GPU slate that maps to a couple hosting strategies (private deployment + reserved dedicated pool). Can you confirm procurement timeline constraints? Two internal delivery options we're considering:

A) Private deployment (on-prem/VPC) with dedicated GPU pool owned by MedCore — longer procurement lead, higher up-front OPEX/CAPEX but full isolation.
B) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in our compliant cloud region) — faster onboarding, committed monthly contract, Redwood manages the fleet and provides SLA and compliance controls.

If procurement needs to be completed inside 8 weeks we should price B as primary and present A as a transition path (MedCore owns hardware later). If MedCore prefers to own from Day 1 we’ll align procurement steps and a longer ramp.

Quick asks:
- Can procurement commit window be shared? (8-week vs 16-week vs 12+ week)
- Any hard constraints on on-prem hardware (preferred vendor / accelerator type)?

I’ll loop in our solutions and procurement leads once you confirm.

Thanks,
Jordan
Enterprise GTM | Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming: MedCore's procurement prefers to avoid hardware ownership unless absolutely required. Primary goal is isolation + auditability; owning hardware is acceptable if it shortens compliance sign-off, but the CISO has asked for the minimal timeline to reach SOC 2-ready state.

Timeline constraints: our procurement cycle can do a fast-track in ~10 weeks if we accept a Redwood-managed dedicated offering with specific contractual security addenda. If we need to source vendors and do POs for hardware, add 6–8 weeks procurement + rack/infra lead time (so 16–18 weeks total).

Accelerator: CISO flagged that H100-class or equivalently validated 80GB alternatives are preferred for our model precision and performance. Quantization strategy needs to preserve top-3 accuracy for core clinical prompts.

Can you sketch a bridge plan that starts Redwood Dedicated (to hit 10-week target) and transitions to private ownership later, while preserving data isolation guarantees? Also want to see a blended cost estimate for first 12 months with both options.

Sanjay

Jordan / Marissa —

Quick sizing and assumptions (short form):
- Traffic profile: 45M tokens/day, 12k qps peak (interactive short prompts avg 60 tokens), 1k nightly batch jobs (avg 1500 tokens).
- Working model: mix of low-latency routing (online pods) + batch nodes for nightly bulk.

Recommended Dedicated-start slate (to meet 10-week onboarding):
- Online pool: 8 nodes @ H100-80GB equiv (continuous batching enabled, KV cache warmers). Estimated sustained p95 ~ 90–120ms for 60-token interactive prompts.
- Batch pool: 4 nodes @ A100-80GB (cost-efficient for throughput, can accept slightly higher latency for batch jobs).
- Cache layer: Redis cluster + persistent S3 prefix for KV snapshotting (ensure KV snapshots exported daily).

Estimated committed throughput capacity: ~6M tokens/day per H100 node (with our batching and cache assumptions), hence 8 nodes ~= 48M tokens/day headroom for growth.

Blended 12-month cost estimate (very high level):
- Path 1 (Dedicated-first then private migration at month 4):
  * Months 1–4: Redwood Dedicated committed (8 H100 + 4 A100) => committed spend ~$430k/month (includes reserved capacity discount, 24/7 ops, SOC2 addendum).
  * Migration month (month 4): one-time migration services fee ~$120k (data transfer, KV continuity, cutover testing).
  * Months 5–12: Customer-owned private infra ops cost ~= amortized infra + support ~$210k/month (reduced vendor margin; includes rack, networking, KMS ops).
  * Year 1 total: approximately $3.2M (includes migration fee).

- Path 2 (Private-from-Day-1):
  * Procurement + hardware lead time: 16 weeks; POs + install one-time capital ~$1.8M (hardware + racks + initial services).
  * Month 1–12 ops + support: ~$220k/month.
  * Year 1 total (including capex amortized over 12 months): approximately $4.5M (higher up-front).

Contract/SLA notes for staged migration:
- While on Redwood Dedicated we can offer a compliant-presence addendum: isolated tenancy per customer, audit logs exported, KMS attestation — this maps 1:1 to many of MedCore's controls.
- During migration, we maintain KV snapshot exports and ensure tokenization keys are rotated with customer KMS. Network cutover requires scheduled maintenance window with <2 hour expected downtime for cutover testing.
- After private cutover, Redwood will provide an ops playbook and optionally a managed-support retainer for 6 months. SLA terms change: Redwood Dedicated carries a 99.9% regionally-backed uptime SLA; Private will be subject to mutually agreed operational responsibilities (hardware uptime vs Redwood-managed control plane).

I can produce a slide with a few sensitivity scenarios (e.g., 20% higher peak qps, or +2x batch jobs) if helpful.

- Irene

Team —

Irene's numbers look reasonable. A few additions from procurement/legal perspective before we send to MedCore:

1) Offer a staged credit: if MedCore signs a 12-month committed Dedicated contract and migrates to private infra within 6 months, offer a migration credit equal to 30% of months 1–3 committed fees (applied toward migration services). This reduces upfront cash for them and incentivizes the staged path.
2) DocuSign flow: two parallel agreements — (A) Dedicated commitment (month-to-month volume + 12-month commitment with SOC2 addendum) and (B) Migration & Services SOW (one-time). We need Procurement contact to confirm PO process; ask Sanjay if they issue blanket PO for services vs hardware.
3) SLA language: include explicit fallback policy to Redwood-hosted fallback in the SOW during cutover with a runbook and rollback test.

Jordan — pls send Sanjay a short executive note summarizing the two paths, high-level costs (Irene's top-line), and the staged credit offer. Ask for procurement cadence and whether they can start a 10-week fast-track approval for Dedicated.

I'll draft the contract bullets after we get their cadence.
